**Orbweaver 1.0.1 makes Orbweaver a full client for OpenClaw agents, and lets you arrange orbs into your own groups.** It also adds a global mute, custom usage orbs and a pool of personas for agent teams, and fixes a set of bugs found since 1.0.0.

## OpenClaw: a full client, not only a viewer

Before this release, Orbweaver showed the conversations OpenClaw agents were having on Discord and WhatsApp. It now also works with an agent's own sessions, the way the gateway's own clients do.

- **An agent's own sessions as orbs.** An agent's main session and chats you start with **New Chat** can have orbs, controlled by the new **Agents' own sessions** setting (Hidden, With chats, or their own diamond-shaped group). Discord and WhatsApp conversations keep the orbs they had.
- **Keep on screen and Rename.** An orb's menu can pin a conversation, which every OpenClaw client then sees, and rename it. A pinned conversation no longer times out, and New Chat conversations stay until you end them.
- **Replies stream live.** An open chat panel shows a reply as the agent writes it, and each tool call as one line. History reads the same however far you scroll back, with no lost, repeated or doubled lines or pictures.
- **Run controls for an agent's own sessions:** model, thinking, fast mode and a time limit, each with a Default choice, plus picture attachments. You get a note when a run hits its limit. Discord and WhatsApp conversations don't get these controls.
- **Approve an agent's actions from Orbweaver.** Turn on **Allow approving agent actions** in Settings. A pending approval turns its orb amber, even if that conversation's orb is hidden, and the chat panel shows the request and names the agent, with **Deny** and **Allow once**. Only a deliberate click answers an approval. There's no keyboard path, and "allow always" is never offered. A request with unsafe characters or an over-long command can only be denied.
- **Replies in an agent's own session stay there.** They're no longer delivered to a chat surface. Discord and WhatsApp conversations send exactly as before.
- **Videos and attachments.** A video an agent posts draws as a tile that opens in your system player, including a clip that one agent made and another delivered. Every attachment kind the gateway sends now draws, and the panel says plainly when the gateway couldn't deliver one.
- **WhatsApp.** A group is badged and titled as a group by its name. No orb title shows a raw phone number or id, on any surface. The gateway's own notices ("Exec completed", reminders, `System:` lines) draw as notes instead of as your words.
- **A bad string from the gateway can no longer freeze every orb.**
- **Media fetches use this device's own operator token**, not the gateway's shared secret, so Orbweaver holds no more access over HTTP than its pairing grants.

## Orb groups

- **Snap orbs into your own groups.** Drag an orb near another orb, or near a group's outline, to snap it in. Drag it away to take it out. Each group gets its own shape and place on screen. Groups never overlap each other or pinned orbs, and they're remembered across restarts.
- **Agent teams move together.** Dragging a team lead moves the whole team, and a member you drag keeps its spot relative to the lead.
- **Group names can be shown or hidden.** Joining, leaving and dropping are animated. With your system's reduce-motion setting on, every movement is a plain short glide.
- The heartbeat and cron clusters are now predefined groups, and their shapes carry over.

## Everything else

- **Global mute.** One switch silences every sound Orbweaver makes: spoken replies and the chimes. Use **Mute** in the tray menu, **Ctrl+Alt+M** (rebindable), or the speaker button in any chat panel's header. While muted, the tray icon shows a slash.
- **Customize a usage orb.** Right-click a usage orb and choose **Customize…** to give it its own initials, name and icon. You can also do this from that account's row in Settings. Icons come from a local PNG, JPEG or SVG file. An SVG that links to files outside itself is refused.
- **A pool of personas for agent teams.** Keep personas in a shared pool (`~/.orbweaver` by default), give them roles, group them into teams, and put a team on a task with the bundled `orbweaver-team` skill. Each teammate gets its own name and orb, instead of every teammate wearing the main session's face. The installers set the skill up on macOS and Windows.
- **A team started from Claude Code in WSL is drawn as a team**, with arrows to its lead, instead of as unrelated orbs.
- **Usage polling works when Orbweaver inherits `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.** It reads the account it was started under, not `~/.claude`.
- **The Windows installer says it adds no firewall rule.** Its firewall steps never ran on a per-user install. Windows Firewall asks the first time you turn on the peer link, which is off by default.

## Heads-up when upgrading

- **If you hid heartbeat sessions,** an agent's own main session no longer follows "Heartbeat sessions". Those orbs come back under **Agents' own sessions** until you hide that too. Main sessions that a WhatsApp conversation is routed into are still heartbeats.
- **Turning on "Allow approving agent actions" re-pairs this device** with the gateway, because it asks for the approvals permission. Leave it off and nothing about approvals is requested or polled.
- **macOS:** as with every upgrade, re-grant Local Network in System Settings → Privacy & Security if OpenClaw or a remote-control peer stops connecting.

## Known limitations

- A real inbound WhatsApp direct message hasn't been seen on a live gateway, so who sent one isn't attributed.
- The persona pool's WSL install paths have no automated test. A persona file without front matter can't be used by the team skill, though an orb can still read it.
- A paired machine's roster doesn't carry teams from a WSL session.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `Orbweaver-1.0.1-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `Orbweaver-1.0.1-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `Orbweaver-1.0.1-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `OrbweaverSpeech-*.zip` files are the optional neural speech engine. The app downloads the one it needs, so you don't need to.
